findings.text: The lane makes placement selection for a kexec buffer plus purgatory loading and purgatory symbol address resolution available to outside callers. Placement chooses a load base for caller supplied size and bounds, loading prepares the purgatory image from its embedded executable view, and symbol resolution maps a name to its future loaded address.

The lane makes forward and reverse walkers over system memory resources and a descriptor filtered walker over the general memory tree available to outside callers. Each walker accepts an address interval with caller context and a callback, visits matching ranges in order, and propagates callback termination status to stop scanning.

The lane makes generic and task stack specific erasing gates plus a sanitizer depth recording hook available to low level callers. The gates decide internally whether erasing is bypassed and otherwise erase stale stack content, while the depth hook narrows tracked lowest stack for later erasure.
The internal header offers an inline handover placement hook that always reports continuation. Callers therefore proceed to normal allocation when handover specific handling is absent in this build.

Purgatory symbol search requires a present executable view, scans section headers for symbol tables, discards tables whose linked string table is out of range, and within each table only accepts globally bound entries with matching names. A match with undefined or out of range section association is treated as failure with diagnostic output, otherwise the matching entry is returned and absence yields null.

Top directed search begins near the smaller of interval end and caller maximum reduced by requested size with optional randomization, aligns downward, and rejects candidates below interval start or caller minimum. Bottom directed search begins at the larger of interval start and caller minimum with optional randomization, aligns upward, and rejects candidates whose end passes interval end or caller maximum. Both refuse candidates overlapping existing image destinations or architecture excluded spans by stepping a page and retrying, otherwise they store the candidate and request stop.

The hole callback ignores driver managed spans, spans smaller than requested size, and spans wholly outside caller bounds. Surviving spans are handed to top directed or bottom directed search according to caller direction, and the search result decides whether outer scanning continues.

Crash images are confined to their reserved region, while normal images walk free memblock extents or the system memory resource tree depending on build setting and caller direction. Memblock extents are converted from exclusive to inclusive end before callback, iteration ends at first successful callback, and one build variant supplies a disabled walker that always reports no progress.

Resource iteration repeatedly obtains the next matching clipped range inside the remaining interval, invokes the caller callback on it, advances past its end, and stops when the callback requests termination or no match remains. Next match scanning skips nested children until a top level overlapping range appears, then accepts the first type matching entry and returns a copy clipped to requested bounds preserving flags descriptor and parent linkage.

Contiguous reservation is refused for images that forbid it and for crash images. On other images a contiguous attempt sized from requested size and caller alignment is made, reservations overlapping existing destinations are released and reported as busy, otherwise the base and page handle are recorded and architecture code is notified before success is reported.

Overall placement honors a caller preset base first, then consults handover handling where a non positive outcome ends the attempt, then tries contiguous reservation as a fast path, and finally walks resources or memblocks with the hole callback. Walk success maps to overall success and any other walk outcome maps to address unavailable.

Purgatory buffer sizing visits only allocated sections, accumulates file backed and zero fill sizes separately with per section alignment, aligns total file size to zero fill alignment, keeps the larger alignment, derives total memory size as file plus zero fill, allocates the file portion, and on registration failure releases the allocation and clears the stored pointer.

Section setup copies headers to writable storage, places zero fill sections after the file image with alignment while assigning runtime addresses, places file backed allocated sections sequentially with alignment while copying bytes and assigning matching runtime address and file offset, and fixes image start at most once either from a named start symbol in executable content or from containment of the original entry inside executable content.

Relocation handling visits only relocation sections, validates linked symbol table and target indices, skips targets that are not allocated, validates the linked string table index, and delegates each surviving section to an architecture handler chosen by relocation flavor, propagating the first error and otherwise reporting success.

Symbol address resolution reports an invalid argument marker when lookup misses, otherwise it combines the resolved section runtime base with symbol value to yield the future loaded address after segment loading.

The headers archive is presented as a read only binary attribute whose data pointer and length derive from kernel linker symbols at init, creation is attempted beneath the kernel object, and cleanup removes the same attribute.

The erasing control holds an integer toggle bounded between disabled and enabled, delegates parsing and range enforcement to generic integer vector handling, preserves prior state across entry, and only on a changed write updates the global bypass branch and emits a warning naming the new state.

Erasure bypass is governed by a switchable branch in one build and is never bypassed in another. Poisoning writes a fixed pattern word by word over a half open span. Erasure derives the low bound from poison search and tracked lowest, optionally records a metric, chooses the high bound as current pointer on task stack or task top otherwise, poisons that span, and resets tracked lowest to task top for the next entry.

The depth hook aligns the current pointer to word size and narrows tracked lowest only when the aligned value lies inside task bounds and below the current tracked value, with a build time check relating tracking granularity to search depth.
Performance oriented symbol access is allowed only when performance events support is built and the paranoid level is at or below the permissive threshold, otherwise it is denied.
Scanning for the next matching resource holds the global resource read lock across the tree walk and releases it before returning, shielding linkage and range fields during matching and copying.

The placement buffer observed here carries image reference, caller address bounds, size and alignment needs, chosen base, direction flag, contiguous page handle, and file versus memory sizes with staging pointer. Placement reads bounds sizes and flags and writes back base and handle, while purgatory setup initializes alignment sizes and staging pointer.

The resource view exchanged with callbacks carries start and end bounds plus flags descriptor and parent linkage. Walk helpers synthesize clipped copies preserving flags descriptor and parent, while reverse collection stores whole copies for later reverse dispatch.

Purgatory state observed here links an executable header pointer with a writable section header copy and a staging buffer pointer. Setup populates staging then writable headers, relocation uses both header views, and load failure paths clear allocated pointers after release.

Placement search cycles through align candidate, bounds test, destination overlap test, architecture exclusion test, and either record success and exit or step a page and retry. Bounds failure exits with continuation status to try the next range, while success exits with stop status.

Purgatory loading moves from size validation to buffer sizing to section layout to relocation, with failure at sizing ending immediately, failure at layout releasing the staging buffer, and failure at relocation releasing both section copy and staging buffer before reporting the error.

Reverse walking first collects forward matches into a growable list expanded in fixed increments, then dispatches callbacks in reverse order stopping at first termination request, and always releases the list before returning the last callback status or a default failure when collection is empty or interrupted.

A kernel control node for stack erasing is registered at boot with restricted permissions and bounded integer handling, offering the persistent runtime switch observed here for enabling or disabling erasure.

Boot time handling publishes the compressed headers archive as a read only system file and exit time handling unpublishes the same file, forming the full lifecycle of that diagnostic interface as shown.

Callers must expect absent headers, out of range table indices, undefined sections, failed allocations for staging headers buffers contiguous pages and reverse lists, overlapping destinations, and invalid purgatory size, each mapped to null return or negative status with cleanup of partial state where shown.

The fragments use symbolic markers for invalid argument, missing device, out of memory, operation not permitted, device busy, bad executable, and address unavailable to distinguish failures, plus named flags for system memory, busy state, driver managed memory, and descriptor filtering, and a sentinel for unknown placement address.
The internal kexec header defines an include guard marker that records inclusion and prevents repeated inclusion within one translation unit.
